decision: Retain the qualified offline broker and reproducible trace findings. Continue isolated transport/clock/IPC and aggregate-admission integration. Do not deploy the kernel into current collectors or reinterpret existing study receipts.
falsifier: Source/receipt integrity mismatch, early or lost subscriber outcome, duplicate dispatch grant, altered outcome hidden by body-only equality, omitted unknown weight, or representative integrated observations showing latency/correlated-failure costs outweighing the measured opportunity revises the relevant claim. No profitability or live-execution-failure inference is made.
hypothesis: Explicitly opted-in exact-payload in-flight sharing can reduce public research request duplication while preserving separate, honest subscriber outcomes and provenance.
limitations: Offline broker kernel and fixed-workload replay; physical transport, IPC, commit and subscriber delivery timing remain unqualified.
One-second earlier-admission sharing requires explicit subscriber/study consent. Same-millisecond strict sharing reflects recorded millisecond resolution.
Replayed body and duration are the observed leader values; real replanning and different future values can change results.
Failure-fanout test shows sharing can worsen a follower outcome; admission does not use future outcome equality.
Initial later window exposed an unsupported transport failure and became development evidence. Fresh ten-minute comparison was separately predeclared and captured after its cutoff.
Unknown response weight is explicit; other-IP traffic and server accounting remain unmeasured.
HTTP status-error and lease-expiry replay still reject explicitly; direct broker controls cover those behaviors separately.
One defensive replay delivery guard remains unexercised; no claim of power-loss resilience, scheduling optimality, market edge or profitability.
All five collectors, financial source/settings/processes and sealed study declarations remain unchanged.
